title: Solving linear equations on the balance
summary: An equation is a balance. Try values, then solve equations with x on one or both sides, fractions and brackets by doing the same to both pans, and change the subject of a formula.
guide: This studio follows KS3 algebra: solving linear equations in one variable, including all forms that need rearrangement, and changing the subject of a formula.
An {{term:equation}} such as {{alg:3x + 2 = 14}} is like a balance: the two sides weigh the same. x is the {{term:unknown}}; the {{term:solution}} is the number that makes both sides equal.
The tiles: a green strip is {{alg:x}}, a yellow square is {{alg:1}}, and a red tile is negative. A white and a red tile of the same shape cancel each other (a zero pair).
The golden rule: whatever you do to one pan, do to the other. A move on one pan only tips the scale.
Choose a move below the scale (add or take away a tile, × or ÷ by a number), then tap a pan, or Both pans. Each level equation is written above the scale, one step under another.

engine.label-pick: Now tap a pan, or Both pans.
engine.label-pick-pan: Now tap a pan, then the other pan.
engine.label-pick-move: First choose a move below the scale.
engine.label-tipped: The scale tipped! Do the same to the other pan.
engine.label-turn: Turn the sign round: tap it.
engine.label-turned: × or ÷ by a negative number turned the sign round.
engine.label-level: Level again: the same move on both pans.
engine.instruction-try: Change x until the scale is level.
engine.instruction-balance: Choose a move, then tap the pans.

try-a-value.title: Is x = 4 a solution?
try-a-value.prompt: Here is {{alg:2x + 5 = 13}}. Is {{alg:x = 4}} a solution? Predict yes or no. Then use − and + to put a value on every x strip and watch the scale. Find the value that makes it level.
try-a-value.hint: With x = 4, the left pan holds 4 + 4 + 5. Is that 13?
try-a-value.success: Yes! With {{alg:x = 4}}, {{alg:4 + 4 + 5 = 13}}, so the scale is level: 4 is the solution.
try-a-value.why: Why does the solution make the scale level, while any other number tips it?
try-a-value.model: The pans weigh the same only when 2x + 5 really is 13. With x = 4 the left pan is 4 + 4 + 5 = 13, the same as the right pan. With x = 5 it is 15, too heavy; with x = 3 it is 11, too light. Only one number balances the scale, and that number is the solution of the equation.

feedback.not-tried: Use + to put a value on the x strips.
feedback.too-big: The left pan is too heavy: try a smaller value.
feedback.too-small: The left pan is too light: try a bigger value.
feedback.coefficient-added: With x = 6, 2x is 6 + 6 = 12, not 2 + 6. The left pan weighs 17: too heavy.

pan-by-pan.title: Solve 3x + 2 = 14, pan by pan
pan-by-pan.prompt: Predict x and type it. Then solve {{alg:3x + 2 = 14}} on the scale: choose a move, tap the left pan, then the right pan. What happens to the scale after your first tap?
pan-by-pan.hint: Choose −1 and take a small square from each pan, twice. Then ÷3 splits each pan into 3 equal groups.
pan-by-pan.success: Well done! {{alg:3x + 2 = 14}} → {{alg:3x = 12}} → {{alg:x = 4}}. Every move was done to both pans, so the scale ended level.
pan-by-pan.why: Why did the scale tip when you changed only one pan?
pan-by-pan.model: Because the two pans were equal, and changing only one made it heavier or lighter than the other. Taking 2 away from both sides keeps them equal: 3x = 12. Dividing both sides by 3 keeps them equal too: x = 4. The same move on both sides keeps an equation true.

feedback.empty: Type your prediction for x on the keypad.
feedback.one-pan: The scale is tipped: one pan has had a move that the other has not. Do the same to the other pan, or Undo.
feedback.constant-left: x is not alone yet: there are small squares with the strips. Take them away from both pans.
feedback.coefficient-left: Three strips are 3x. Split both pans into 3 equal groups: ÷3.
feedback.subtract-coefficient: 3x means 3 × x. Taking 3 away from 12 gives 9, but 12 has to be shared between 3 strips: 12 ÷ 3.
feedback.coefficient-kept: 12 is what 3x weighs, not x. Three strips weigh 12, so how much does one strip weigh?
feedback.multiplied: 3x = 12 means three x's make 12. Multiplying makes it bigger: divide instead.
feedback.wrong-sign-across: Taking 2 from the left pan means taking 2 from the right pan too: 14 − 2, not 14 + 2.
feedback.too-big: Too big. Put your number on the strips in your head: does 3x + 2 make 14?
feedback.too-small: Too small. Put your number on the strips in your head: does 3x + 2 make 14?

unknown-both-sides.title: x on both pans
unknown-both-sides.prompt: Solve {{alg:5x - 3 = 2x + 12}}. There are strips on both pans. Predict x and type it, then solve it on the scale. Which strips will you take away?
unknown-both-sides.hint: Add 3 white squares to both pans: they cancel the 3 red ones on the left. Then take 2 strips from both pans.
unknown-both-sides.why: Why is it easier to take 2 strips from both pans, rather than 5?
unknown-both-sides.model: Taking away the smaller number of strips, 2x, leaves 3x on the left: a positive number of x's. Taking away 5x also works, but it leaves −3x on the right, and at the end you must divide by a negative number. Both ways give x = 5, as long as you do the same to both pans.

feedback.empty: Type your prediction for x on the keypad.
feedback.one-pan: The scale is tipped: one pan has had a move that the other has not. Do the same to the other pan, or Undo.
feedback.unknown-both-sides: There are still strips on both pans. Take away the same number of strips from each pan.
feedback.constant-left: x is not alone yet: there are small squares with the strips. Remove them from both pans.
feedback.coefficient-left: Split both pans into equal groups, one for each strip.
feedback.negative-unknown: You have −x: a red strip. Choose −1 and multiply both pans by it to turn the strip white.
feedback.negative-forgotten: The −3 is three red squares on the left. To cancel them, add 3 to both pans: 12 + 3 = 15, not 12 − 3.
feedback.coefficient-kept: 15 is what 3x weighs. Divide both pans by 3.
feedback.too-big: Too big. Try your number in both sides: are they equal?
feedback.too-small: Too small. Try your number in both sides: are they equal?

undo-a-division.title: Undo a division
undo-a-division.prompt: The short strip is {{alg:x/3}}, a third of x. Solve {{alg:x/3 + 1 = 5}}: predict x, then use the scale. Which move undoes "divide by 3"?
undo-a-division.hint: First take 1 away from both pans. Then multiply both pans by 3: three thirds of x make one x.
undo-a-division.why: Why do you multiply by 3, and not divide, to find x from {{alg:x/3 = 4}}?
undo-a-division.model: {{alg:x/3}} is x divided by 3. Multiplying by 3 undoes dividing by 3: {{alg:x/3 × 3 = x}}. The other pan must be multiplied too: 4 × 3 = 12. Dividing again would give {{alg:x/9}}, a ninth of x, even further from x.

feedback.empty: Type your prediction for x on the keypad.
feedback.one-pan: The scale is tipped: one pan has had a move that the other has not. Do the same to the other pan, or Undo.
feedback.divided-not-multiplied: Dividing again made an even smaller piece of x ({{alg:x/9}}). Undo, then multiply both pans by 3.
feedback.fraction-left: The strip is still only part of x. Multiply both pans by the number under x.
feedback.constant-left: There is still a small square next to the strip. Take it away from both pans.
feedback.fraction-kept: 4 is what {{alg:x/3}} weighs: a third of x. The whole of x is 3 times as much.
feedback.wrong-sign-across: Take 1 away from both sides: 5 − 1 = 4, not 5 + 1.
feedback.one-term-multiplied: Multiplying a pan by 3 multiplies everything on it: {{alg:3(x/3 + 1) = x + 3}}, not {{alg:x + 1}}.
feedback.too-big: Too big. Check: your number ÷ 3, plus 1, should make 5.
feedback.too-small: Too small. Check: your number ÷ 3, plus 1, should make 5.

brackets.title: An equation with brackets
brackets.prompt: In {{alg:2(x + 3) = 16}} the left pan holds 2 equal groups of {{alg:x + 3}}. Predict x, then solve it. Will you split both pans into 2 groups, or open the brackets first?
brackets.hint: Divide both pans by 2: one group, {{alg:x + 3}}, weighs 8.
brackets.success: Well done! {{alg:2(x + 3) = 16}} → {{alg:x + 3 = 8}} → {{alg:x = 5}}. Opening the brackets works too: {{alg:2x + 6 = 16}}.
brackets.why: If you split the left pan into 2 groups, why must you divide 16 by 2 as well?
brackets.model: Two equal groups of x + 3 weigh 16, so one group weighs 16 ÷ 2 = 8: the same move on both pans. Then x + 3 = 8, so x = 5. If you open the brackets instead, the 2 multiplies both terms: 2x + 6 = 16, then 2x = 10 and x = 5.

feedback.empty: Type your prediction for x on the keypad.
feedback.one-pan: The scale is tipped: one pan has had a move that the other has not. Do the same to the other pan, or Undo.
feedback.bracket-left: x is still inside the 2 groups. Divide both pans by 2, or open the brackets.
feedback.constant-left: x is not alone yet. Take the small squares away from both pans.
feedback.coefficient-left: Split both pans into equal groups, one for each strip.
feedback.factor-ignored: There are 2 groups of x + 3, so 2(x + 3) = 16, not x + 3 = 16. Divide the 16 by 2 too.
feedback.stopped-early: 8 is what x + 3 weighs. Take 3 away from both pans.
feedback.wrong-sign-across: x + 3 = 8: take 3 away from both pans, 8 − 3.
feedback.too-big: Too big. Check: (your number + 3) × 2 should make 16.
feedback.too-small: Too small. Check: (your number + 3) × 2 should make 16.

change-the-subject.title: Change the subject of v = u + at
change-the-subject.prompt: The formula {{alg:v = u + at}} gives a speed. Make t the subject: get t on its own on one pan, with the same moves as for equations. The letter tiles stand for numbers.
change-the-subject.hint: Take u away from both pans. Then divide both pans by a.
change-the-subject.success: Well done! {{alg:v = u + at}} → {{alg:v - u = at}} → {{alg:(v - u)/a = t}}, so {{alg:t = (v - u)/a}}.
change-the-subject.why: Why is it {{alg:t = (v - u)/a}} and not {{alg:t = v - u/a}}?
change-the-subject.model: Dividing a pan by a divides everything on it, so the whole of v − u goes over a. Writing {{alg:v - u/a}} would divide only the u: a different formula, and the scale would tip. The order of moves is the same as for 2x + 1 = 7: first take away, then divide.

feedback.one-pan: The scale is tipped: one pan has had a move that the other has not. Do the same to the other pan, or Undo.
feedback.constant-left: There is still a u with the at tile. Take u away from both pans.
feedback.coefficient-left: at means a × t. Divide both pans by a to leave t on its own.
feedback.unknown-both-sides: t is on both pans. Undo and start with the u.
feedback.fraction-left: t is under a bar. Multiply both pans by a.
